job.title: Instructional Designer
job.description:
Instructional Designer, Client Services Learning & Development

About the role

We are hiring our first dedicated Instructional Designer to build Learning & Development for our Client Services group from the ground up. This is a full-scope role: you will design the curriculum, select and launch the training platform, write the content, deliver the training, and prove its impact with measurable results.
Client Services is growing quickly, and our first priority is getting new hires to full productivity faster and more consistently. Today, much of how the work gets done lives with the experienced team members already in the role. You will capture that knowledge, turn it into standardized procedures, and build a repeatable onboarding program around it.
Standardized procedure documentation is central to this role, especially for the Form CRS (Customer Relationship Summary) and the client-facing processes tied to it. Your work will help ensure every client interaction is accurate, consistent, and compliant.

Key responsibilities

Build the L&D function

  • Assess current Client Services skills, workflows, and knowledge gaps through interviews, job shadowing, and process reviews with tenured team members and leadership.
  • Design the L&D strategy, governance, and operating model for Client Services, including roadmap, priorities, and success metrics.
  • Build a structured new-hire onboarding curriculum with defined learning paths, milestones, and competency checkpoints.
  • Establish standards and templates for all training and procedure content so materials stay consistent as the team scales.

Select and launch the training platform

  • Define requirements, evaluate vendors, and recommend a Learning Management System (LMS) or learning platform.
  • Lead implementation: configuration, course and user setup, enrollment rules, reporting, and integrations with HR and other firm systems.
  • Serve as platform administrator and owner, maintaining content, user records, and completion tracking.

Standardize procedures, including Form CRS

  • Document Client Services procedures as clear, step-by-step standard operating procedures (SOPs), job aids, and checklists.
  • Own procedure documentation related to the Form CRS (Customer Relationship Summary), including delivery requirements, timing, client communication, and recordkeeping.
  • Partner with Compliance to ensure training and procedures align with SEC, FINRA, and firm requirements, and update content when rules or processes change.
  • Maintain a version-controlled procedure library that serves as the single source of truth for the team.

Develop and deliver training

  • Apply adult learning principles and instructional design models (ADDIE, SAM, or similar) to create blended learning: eLearning, instructor-led sessions, virtual training, simulations, and on-the-job practice.
  • Build content with authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Adobe Captivate, or Camtasia.
  • Facilitate onboarding and ongoing training sessions, both in person in Chicago and virtually.
  • Design a mentoring or peer-shadowing program that pairs new hires with experienced team members.

Measure and improve

  • Define and track outcome metrics such as time to proficiency, error rates, quality scores, client satisfaction, and new-hire retention.
  • Use evaluation frameworks such as the Kirkpatrick model to assess learning effectiveness and business impact.
  • Report results to Client Services and firm leadership, and continuously refine programs based on data and feedback.

Required qualifications

  • 10+ years of instructional design and L&D experience, with a track record of standing up training programs from the ground up.
  • Wealth management industry experience is required; broader financial services experience is a strong complement.
  • Full-lifecycle ownership: needs analysis, curriculum design, content development, facilitation, program management, and evaluation.
  • Proven, measurable results, such as reduced time to proficiency, improved quality or accuracy, or higher retention. Please be ready to share specific examples.
  • Hands-on experience selecting, implementing, and administering an LMS.
  • Strong procedure-writing skills, with experience producing SOPs and job aids in a regulated environment.
  • Working knowledge of Form CRS, Regulation Best Interest, and related client disclosure and recordkeeping requirements.
  • Confident facilitator for both live and virtual audiences.
  • Able to work hybrid from our Chicago office.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

Preferred qualifications

  • Prior experience in a Client Services, operations, or client service associate role at an RIA, broker-dealer, or private wealth firm.
  • Familiarity with custodial platforms (such as Schwab, Fidelity, or Pershing) and CRM systems (such as Salesforce or Redtail).
  • Certification such as ATD's CPTD, or an instructional design certificate.
  • FINRA licenses (such as SIE or Series 7) or other industry credentials.
  • Experience designing training for teams in rapid growth or scaling phases.

What success looks like in year one

Timeframe Outcome

First 90 days Needs assessment complete; L&D roadmap approved; core Client Services procedures, including Form CRS, documented and reviewed by Compliance

6 months Training platform live; new-hire onboarding program launched with defined learning paths and competency checkpoints

12 months Baseline and improvement reported on time to proficiency, quality, and retention; full procedure library maintained and in use

Pay: $60 to $70 per hour

job.title: Senior Research Program Manager, Survey Operations
job.description:
Senior Research Program Manager, Survey Operations

Contract Duration: 6 months
Employment Type: Full-time Contract

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Senior Research Program Manager, Survey Operations to join our Quantitative Research team on a six-month contract.

In this role, you will design and build the operational model, infrastructure, and governance needed to enable researchers across the organization to conduct survey research independently and responsibly. The initial focus will be on launching a pilot program for experienced Product Researchers.

Working closely with Research Operations, Quantitative Research, UX Research, and cross-functional partners, you will establish the tools, processes, standards, and guidance needed to ensure survey research remains high-quality, compliant, and respectful of customer time as access expands.

Your expertise in end-to-end survey research and operational management will be essential in defining research standards, developing practical playbooks, and implementing the checks and controls that enable researchers to launch studies with confidence.

About the Team

The Research team supports product, marketing, and business decision-making through multi-method research, helping the organization better understand and connect with its customers.

The Quantitative Research team leads key tracking programs, cross-marketplace research, and attitudinal measurement standards. The team is evolving toward a more collaborative model in which survey research becomes a shared capability across Quantitative, Market, and UX Research.

This role will play a key part in building the operational foundation, governance, and resources needed to support that transition.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build survey operations infrastructure: Partner with Research Operations to establish survey tooling configurations, account structures, permissions, naming conventions, and access request workflows.
  • Develop a centralized survey registry: Design and implement a portfolio registry that tracks planned, active, and completed studies and integrates with pre-launch review processes.
  • Establish sample and customer-contact governance: Operationalize sample availability rules, suppression workflows, contact frequency limits, protected programs, and coordination processes for overlapping studies.
  • Define privacy and data governance standards: Collaborate with Legal and Privacy teams to establish baseline requirements for personally identifiable information (PII), consent language, data storage, retention, and escalation for additional review.
  • Create research playbooks and onboarding: Develop practical documentation covering survey programming, quality assurance, launch procedures, monitoring, incident management, escalation pathways, and mandatory research standards.
  • Support researcher qualification and enablement: Work with Quantitative and UX Research teams to translate researcher qualification criteria into practical assessment materials, including applied exercises, scoring rubrics, and debrief guides.
  • Establish governance and escalation frameworks: Define which situations require mandatory escalation, such as customer contact, privacy concerns, protected programs, and launch issues, versus those that warrant optional methodological consultation.
  • Evaluate and scale the pilot program: Support pilot measurement and evaluation, identify opportunities for improvement, and develop recommendations for broader implementation, including reusable templates, question banks, and other shared resources.
  • Drive continuous improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, strengthen operational controls, and improve the overall efficiency and accessibility of survey research.

Responsibilities may evolve over the course of the engagement based on business needs and program priorities.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of relevant experience spanning both primary survey research and survey operations management.
  • End-to-end survey research expertise, including questionnaire design, sampling, weighting, survey programming, analysis, and reporting, with the ability to translate technical expertise into clear standards and guidance for other researchers.

Pay: $64 to $67 per hour

This is a remote, work from home position. This role is to be filled outside the states of California and Colorado.

job.description:
Social Content & TikTok Lead

Overview

Independent creative entrepreneurs are at the heart of our marketplace, building businesses, developing brands, and creating communities of their own. This role plays a key part in supporting and celebrating their success.

As the Social Content & TikTok Lead, you will build and launch a seller-focused TikTok channel from the ground up, defining its strategy, creative direction, and voice. You will establish a distinctive presence on one of today’s most influential cultural platforms, creating content that educates, entertains, and connects with sellers. In addition, you will serve as a hands-on creative partner to the broader social team, contributing video production, editing, and short-form content across seller-focused channels.

Through practical education, timely insights, compelling seller stories, and culturally relevant storytelling, you will develop content that helps sellers grow their businesses, connect with one another, and feel part of a larger community.

This role sits within Seller Marketing, a team focused on empowering sellers and building lasting relationships through education, community engagement, seller milestones, and meaningful storytelling. TikTok and short-form video are key opportunities to bring this mission to life and reach sellers at scale.

This is a true zero-to-one opportunity. You will build the channel’s strategy and go-to-market plan, establish its content pillars and creative identity, and own execution from concept development and filming through editing and publishing. You will have the autonomy to experiment, establish best practices, and shape the channel’s long-term direction.

The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with exceptional creative execution. You bring go-to-market experience, a strong understanding of Gen Z audiences and TikTok culture, and the ability to independently produce high-quality, engaging short-form video from day one.

What You’ll Do

Channel Strategy, Launch & Go-to-Market

  • Develop and launch a seller-focused TikTok channel, defining its purpose, positioning, target audience, and go-to-market strategy.
  • Establish content pillars and a distinctive creative point of view that educates, entertains, and celebrates sellers in a way that feels authentic to TikTok.
  • Translate broader Seller Marketing priorities—including seller education, community building, business growth, and milestone celebrations—into content that audiences find valuable and engaging.
  • Define a channel voice that is approachable, human, seller-first, and authentic while remaining culturally relevant and attention-grabbing.
  • Build a testing and learning roadmap for the first 6–12 months, using audience insights and engagement data to identify content-market fit and guide channel growth.
  • Continuously refine the channel strategy based on performance, audience behavior, emerging trends, and new platform opportunities.

Content Creation & Video Editing

  • Independently develop concepts, film, and edit a high volume of polished short-form videos, owning the creative process from initial idea through final delivery.
  • Create a diverse content mix, including educational tutorials, relatable seller-life content, seller spotlights, success stories, milestone celebrations, product and feature launches, and timely cultural trends.
  • Transform business insights, practical advice, and authentic seller experiences into content that is both informative and entertaining.
  • Build streamlined production workflows that support consistent, high-quality output while allowing the team to respond quickly to opportunities.
  • Film and direct yourself and others as needed, and collaborate with external creators, contractors, and seller partners to bring concepts to life while maintaining a cohesive creative vision.

TikTok Culture & Trendspotting

  • Stay current on TikTok trends, sounds, formats, creators, and cultural conversations, identifying opportunities to engage audiences in relevant and timely ways.

job.title: Investments Risk, Principal
job.description:
Quantitative Investments Risk Associate (Hedge Funds)


Company Overview


Our client is a premier global alternative asset management firm with a highly respected investments platform. Their established Investments Risk team has built out the firm's core proprietary risk and attribution models, optimization frameworks, alpha analysis, and client reporting infrastructure. They are seeking an experienced professional to help shape investment and portfolio decisions across the firm's hedge fund activity.


Position Overview


In this role, you will use quantitative risk analysis—including alpha decomposition, stress testing, and optimization—to inform manager evaluation, position sizing, and asset allocation. You will build and apply the risk tools and analytics underlying this work, contributing to both internal risk oversight and external investor reporting.


This position offers a high degree of autonomy. While much of the work is well-defined, you will have the opportunity to identify problems worth solving on your own initiative, evolve existing infrastructure, and design roadmaps for unresolved challenges.


Schedule: Hybrid (3 days onsite: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday).

Key Responsibilities

  • Quantitative Risk Modeling: Build and maintain quantitative risk models and analytics (including factor and alpha decomposition, stress testing, and scenario analysis) working with large, structured datasets (SQL, data lakes) and using Python.
  • Portfolio Construction & Analysis: Support manager evaluation and investment decisions by conducting portfolio risk monitoring and asset allocation analysis.
  • Market Monitoring: Track and interpret risk exposures, factor trends, and capital market conditions relevant to specific hedge fund strategies.
  • Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner with portfolio managers and the Investment Committee on portfolio construction decisions.
  • Reporting & Presentation: Design and deliver polished risk and performance presentations for internal oversight and external investor transparency requests.

Requirements & Experience

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics/Econometrics, Financial Engineering) or equivalent technical experience.
  • Experience: 3 to 7 years of experience in investment analysis, risk management, or asset allocation, ideally with exposure to hedge fund or absolute return strategies.
  • Technical Skills: Proficiency in Python and hands-on experience working with large structured datasets. Comfort using AI-assisted tools where appropriate is a plus.
  • Communication: Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to translate complex quantitative analysis into clear, actionable conclusions for investment committees and clients.
  • Presentation: Strong skills in building and delivering highly polished materials in PowerPoint or other reporting formats.
  • Initiative: A self-starter mentality with the judgment and ownership to operate effectively in environments where directions are not always fully specified.

Pay: $175,000 to $215,000 per year

Benefits: medical, dental, vision and life insurance, flexible spending accounts, an employer sponsored retirement plan, paid time off, parental leave, and short and long-term disability.

job.title: Cloud and Automation Engineer
job.description:
The Cloud and Infrastructure team owns and operates the systems that power the business: Azure, on-premises hyperconverged infrastructure, and the networking and telephony that connect them. We are growing the team to reduce single points of ownership, build deeper coverage across our platforms, and shift more of our work from manual support toward engineering, automation, and self-service.


We're looking for a Cloud and Automation Engineer who thinks in systems, not just tools. You should be comfortable moving between cloud and on-premises environments, understand how infrastructure, identity, networking, and applications depend on one another, and be driven to replace repetitive manual work with code and process. You'll work as part of cross-functional squads alongside engineering, security, and business partners, so strong collaboration and communication matter as much as technical depth.


This role is well suited to someone who has built real depth in systems and cloud engineering, who is genuinely energized by learning new platforms and approaches, and who wants to help mature a team's practices rather than just execute a backlog. This role is on a hybrid schedule, with office presence expected two days per week.


Responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and operate infrastructure across Azure and on-premises hyperconverged environments, applying consistent engineering principles regardless of platform.
  • Automate provisioning, configuration, and operational tasks using infrastructure-as-code practices, reducing manual and repetitive work across the environment.
  • Partner with cross-functional squads to translate business and application requirements into resilient, secure, and maintainable infrastructure designs.
  • Co-design systems and platforms with application developers, favoring immutable infrastructure patterns so environments are consistently rebuilt from code rather than patched or drifted over time.
  • Contribute to the evolution of our hybrid cloud strategy: helping decide what belongs in the private data center versus Azure, and building the automation that makes those workloads portable and consistently managed.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve complex issues that span cloud, virtualization, storage, networking, and identity layers.
  • Establish and document standards, patterns, and runbooks that reduce tribal knowledge and make systems easier for the team to support.
  • Embed SRE principles and engineering practices into how systems are built and how the team works day to day, favoring measurable reliability, proactive detection, and repeatable process over reactive firefighting.
  • Identify opportunities to insource work currently handled by external managed-service partners, and build the automation and monitoring needed to support it internally.
  • Contribute to shifting the team's focus away from bespoke, hand-managed infrastructure and toward *aaS models and reusable, codified platforms, freeing capacity to focus on the systems that enable differentiated business capabilities.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation and incident response, contributing to root-cause analysis and durable fixes rather than one-off remediation.
  • Stay current with evolving cloud, virtualization, and automation practices, and bring new approaches back to the team.

Requirements:


Experience

  • A solution-oriented systems engineering mindset, paired with continuous improvement and being easy to work with across teams.
  • 5-10 years of demonstrated experience integrating and automating infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code approaches, in a public cloud (Azure preferred) and in a virtualized or hyperconverged on-premises environment.
  • A track record of solving problems that cross multiple layers of the stack, not just working within a single platform or tool.
  • Experience working in cross-functional or squad-based delivery models, partnering with engineers, architects, and business stakeholders outside your immediate team.

Skills and Approach

  • Demonstrated experience with Terraform and Ansible, ideally applied in an Azure environment.
  • Strong grounding in core systems and cloud engineering principles: availability, scalability, security, cost, and operability, and the ability to reason about trade-offs between them.
  • A builder's mindset: default to automating and codifying solutions rather than performing repeated manual work.
  • A drive to optimize and re-engineer processes where it makes sense, rather than simply automating what's done today as-is.
  • Comfort operating across a hybrid environment, understanding how workload placement decisions affect cost, performance, resiliency, and support burden.
  • Strong troubleshooting instincts and the ability to work back from symptoms to root cause across interdependent systems.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to document designs and standards that other engineers can follow.
  • A genuine appetite for learning: comfortable picking up new platforms, tools, and practices as the environment evolves, rather than anchoring to a fixed toolset.
  • Good judgment about when to build, when to buy, and when to simplify rather than automate around unnecessary complexity.
  • A reuse- and security-first mindset, applied in a way that keeps sight of user and developer experience rather than adding friction for its own sake.

Nice to Have

  • Exposure to identity and access management, networking, or telephony systems in addition to core infrastructure.
  • Experience contributing to architecture decisions or documentation (e.g., ADRs) rather than only implementing them.
  • Familiarity with reducing reliance on outsourced managed services through internal automation and tooling.
  • Experience working in a highly regulated financial services environment, including familiarity with the risk, compliance, and change-control expectations common there.

Pay: $145,000 to $175,000 per year

Benefits: medical, dental and vision coverage, an employer HSA contribution, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, company paid long-term disability, a 401(k) with match, pre-tax commuter accounts, student loan assistance, tuition reimbursement, vacation and flex time, parental and family leave, and back-up child and elder care.

job.title: Cybersecurity Lead Engineer /Architect
job.description:
The Cybersecurity Lead Engineer/Architect is the firm’s most senior individual contributor in security, joining a lean security operations team responsible for the continued evolution, design, and advancement of the firm’s cybersecurity program. This role deliberately blends high-level strategy and security architecture direction with hands-on implementation engineering: setting the technical vision, reference architectures, and standards while personally building, configuring, and hardening the controls that bring them to life. The role safeguards the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of firm data and systems in alignment with organizational policies and regulatory expectations, leading the design and implementation of security architecture, controls, and technical solutions across the enterprise while proactively identifying risks and recommending strategic improvements.

This individual operates as a highly self-directed contributor within a team responsible for cybersecurity and enterprise risk. The role requires independent assessment of emerging threats, evaluation of control effectiveness, prioritization of initiatives, and ownership of security-focused projects and architectural roadmaps from concept through execution. The Cybersecurity Lead Engineer/Architect regularly collaborates with infrastructure, software engineering, and service desk teams to drive measurable improvements in the firm’s security posture.

As an onsite/hybrid employee, you are expected to be in the office on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursday.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Architect, design, implement, and continuously enhance security controls across endpoint, network, cloud, identity, and SDLC, operating hands-on from design through deployment and tuning.
  • Lead security-focused projects, including scoping, planning, execution, stakeholder communication, and documentation.
  • Own and optimize core security tooling (Application security, AI security, endpoint protection, IDS/IPS, SIEM, vulnerability management, cloud security, etc.), ensuring effective configuration and continuous improvement.
  • Develop and implement automation to enhance threat detection, alerting, response workflows, ticket creation, and reporting metrics.
  • Partner with cross-functional technology teams to embed secure design principles and hardening standards into infrastructure, cloud platforms, and application development (DevSecOps).
  • Lead the firm’s AI security program, establishing governance, guardrails, and technical controls that secure the enterprise’s adoption and use of AI
  • Partner with product and software engineering teams to enable secure AI engineering and development, embedding threat modeling, secure-by-design patterns, and safeguards.
  • Monitor compliance with cybersecurity policies and regulatory requirements; identify gaps and drive remediation efforts.
  • Serve as a technical escalation point during incident response and contribute to post-incident analysis and control improvements.
  • Identify emerging threats, tools, and technologies and recommend strategic direction for the cybersecurity program.

EDUCATION, SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity or information security engineering roles, including time in a lead, principal, or security architect capacity.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing and engineering security controls in enterprise environments.
  • Experience leading or independently managing technical security projects.
  • Strong familiarity with CIS Framework and system hardening standards.
  • Hands-on experience securing and monitoring cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, etc.).
  • Deep understanding of common security controls including DLP, MFA, encryption, intrusion detection, and mobile device/application management.
  • Strong scripting and automation skills (PowerShell, Python, or similar) with software engineering experience preferred
  • Experience designing and maintaining centralized logging and SIEM solutions.
  • Ability to independently assess risk, define problems, and implement practical, scalable solutions.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to influence stakeholders and represent the security function effectively.
  • Proven experience designing enterprise security architecture and reference architectures, balancing strategic, roadmap-level direction with hands-on implementation.
  • Experience securing AI/ML systems and enterprise AI adoption, including familiarity with AI-specific risks (e.g., prompt injection, data leakage, model abuse) and frameworks such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.
  • Experience threat modeling and partnering with software and product engineering teams to enable secure AI and application development.
  • Experience in financial services or investment management preferred.
  • Relevant security certifications (CISSP, CISM, GIAC, AWS Security, etc.) are a plus.

Pay: $150,000 to $200,000 per year

Benefits: medical, dental, vision and life insurance, flexible spending accounts, an employer sponsored retirement plan, paid time off, parental leave, and short and long-term disability.
